subject: Renewal: term rework and invoice timing for BlueOak Systems
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@blueoak.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueOak Systems Procurement <procurements@blueoak.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: price hold + invoice cadence

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you had a good week. Our renewal is up in July and usage is tracking ~25% higher than last year. Procurement asked me to open a short discussion about two items we need to lock down before we can proceed:

1) A 12-month price hold through our renewal period — critical for forecasting with our Q3 budget.
2) Invoice timing aligned to our fiscal quarter (we need invoices to start on July 1) so the spend hits the right ledger.

We're also looking at modest expansion (additional capacity for search and reranking). Before I loop Procurement formally, can your team confirm whether you can accommodate a price hold tied to a committed floor and whether you support a July 1 invoice cadence? If you have a template or an options sheet, please send it over.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueOak Systems

P.S. Procurement requested an updated statement of work and a line-item proposal for the uplift + any one-time onboarding credits.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@blueoak.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@blueoak.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: price hold + invoice cadence

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short options packet and an SOW draft (see attachments). High level — we can support a price hold if the renewal includes a minimum committed capacity. Two options we typically offer:

Option A — Commit + Price Hold (recommended for budget predictability)
- 12 month price hold if customer commits to a minimum monthly committed token-hours (MCTH).
- Renewal discount applied immediately on signed commit.
- Burst credits for overage available as a one-time bucket at contract start.

Option B — Flexible usage with buffer credits (recommended if you want low upfront commitment)
- No price hold guarantee.
- Purchase buffer credits (prepaid) to reduce marginal cost during spikes.
- Quarterly re-evaluation and short-term uplift options.

Two quick clarifications we need from Procurement to draft the amendment properly: approximate target committed baseline (token-hours/month) and desired invoice start date (you mentioned July 1). Can we schedule a 30-minute call Monday to align on numbers? I’m available 9–11am PT.

Attachments: 2027-04-09-Redwood-Proposal-BlueOak-v3.pdf (proposal, 4 pages), SOW-BlueOak-AnnexA.xlsx (line-item matrix)

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
e: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | m: 415-555-0139

From: Luis Moreno <luis.m@blueoak.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@blueoak.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: price hold + invoice cadence

Evelyn — thanks for the options. Procurement and Finance talked this morning; a couple points from our side:

- We are comfortable with a minimum committed baseline, but Procurement needs the ability to shift up to 20% of the committed capacity month-to-month without triggering penalty (we have unpredictable seasonal spikes).
- The invoice cadence must start on July 1 to match our fiscal year; we will accept net 30 payment terms but invoices need to be dated to Q3.
- We'd like a 150k token-hour burst credit bucket included at contract start (to avoid emergency overage charges during early migration).

If you can make the commit flexible in the way described (reassignment up to 20% monthly) and include the burst bucket, we can proceed with final procurement review quickly.

-Luis
Luis Moreno
Senior Procurement Manager
BlueOak Systems

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion: price hold + invoice cadence — internal recommendation

Team — forwarding BlueOak's asks. Quick recommendation before I reply to Luis:

Proposed commercially viable position (balanced for revenue and risk):
- Offer a 12-month price hold conditioned on a minimum commit of 450k token-hours over the year (37.5k token-hours/month average).
- Include an up-front 150k token-hour burst credit bucket, one-time at contract start (non-refundable, applies to overage).
- Permitted reallocation: allow customer to reassign up to 20% of the committed monthly allocation month-to-month, subject to a 5% reprice on any reallocated usage that results in a materially higher peak (>120% of baseline in any month). This preserves predictability while giving them flexibility.
- Invoice timing: we can align billing to July 1 if procurement accepts a short pro-forma adjustment (we will date the initial invoice July 1 and set Net 30). Operations/Revenue: confirm this doesn't break recognition rules.

Questions:
- David: can RevOps handle the reallocation rules and the 5% reprice automation?
- Monica: confirm the accounting treatment of an invoice dated July 1 but with services starting earlier for transition (would we need a contract amendment?).
- Markus/Kim: please advise on language for the reallocation clause and the burst credit bucket so Procurement can accept without legal redlines.

I'll propose this to BlueOak if we get the all-clear.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@blueoak.com>, Luis Moreno <luis.m@blueoak.com>, BlueOak Systems Procurement <procurements@blueoak.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: price hold + invoice cadence — Redwood formal offer

Samantha / Luis — thanks for the clarity and for moving quickly. Based on internal alignment, here is our formal offer for the upcoming renewal:

Summary of commercial terms (final offer):
- 12-month price hold through your 2027 renewal in exchange for a committed annual baseline of 450,000 token-hours (equivalent to an average 37,500 token-hours/month).
- One-time burst credit bucket of 150,000 token-hours applied at contract start to cover early migration spikes or seasonal bursts.
- Flex reallocation: Customer may reassign up to 20% of the committed monthly allocation month-to-month. If reallocation causes any month to exceed 120% of the baseline committed amount, reallocated overage is subject to a 5% surcharge on the per-token-hour rate for that month.
- Renewal discount: 10% applied to base rate for the 12-month term, effective upon signed amendment.
- Invoice schedule: We will align invoices to a July 1 start date per your request. Initial invoice will be issued with a July 1 date and standard Net 30 terms; Redwood Finance will record revenue per standard recognition rules (Monica/finance, cc'd).
- Attachments: updated proposal (2027-04-15-Redwood-Proposal-BlueOak-final.pdf) and a one-click signature link (DocuSign) to expedite procurement.

If these terms are acceptable, please confirm and we will send the finalized amendment and DocuSign. If Procurement needs alternative wording on the reallocation clause, Markus is available to work directly on contract language.
